questions.question: In how many phases did the Indian Economy experience the success of the Green Revolution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Two**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Green Revolution in India experienced success in two phases:**

 
 
• **Phase 1 (1967-1972):-**

 
 
• Introduction of high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds for wheat
 
• Increased production of wheat, particularly in Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh
 
• Transformation of India from a food-deficient to a food-sufficient nation 
 
 
 
• **Phase 2 (1972-1984):-**
 
 
• Expansion of HYV technology to other crops, such as rice, maize, and millet
 
• Wider adoption of HYV seeds across different regions of India
 
• Further increase in agricultural production and food security
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Green Revolution:-**

 
 
• **It was a period of agricultural modernization that began in the 1960s and transformed agriculture in India.**
 
• The Green Revolution** involved** **the introduction of new technologies, such as high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, chemical fertilizers, and pesticides, as well as the expansion of irrigation systems.**
 
• These technologies led to a dramatic increase in agricultural production, particularly for wheat and rice, and helped to India achieve food self-sufficiency.

• In 1879, he bought the newspaper, The Bengalee(founded in 1862 by Girish Chandra Ghosh) and edited it for 40 years in b, when Banerjee was arrested for publishing remarks in his paper.
 
• A Nation in the Making written in the last years of Sir Surendranath Banerjea's life, is not only the autobiography of a pioneering leader in Indian politics but also a commentary on public life.
 
• This book is originally published in 1925.

• Then he formed a committee of three- Triumvirs. Mazzini was one of these Triumvirs. But this young Republic was attacked on all sides: by the Austrians, Neapolitans and the French.

questions.question:
Consider the following list of characteristics and identify the type of forest.

(A) The forests are so thick and receive rainfall throughout the year.

(B) Rosewood, ebony, mahogany are the important trees of these forests.

(C) These forests occur in the regions near the Equator and close to tropics.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is Tropical evergreen forests [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• **Tropical evergreen forests, also known as tropical rainforests, are found in regions near the Equator and close to the tropics, generally between latitudes 10°N and 10°S.**
 
• They are characterized by a warm and wet climate with high annual rainfall, often receiving rainfall throughout the year.
 
• The constant rainfall and high temperatures lead to the growth of lush, dense vegetation, making these forests very thick.
 
• The high humidity and rainfall result in the absence of distinct seasonal changes, which allows trees and plants to grow and retain their leaves year-round, hence the term "evergreen."
 
• Tropical evergreen forests are incredibly diverse and are home to a wide range of plant and animal species, many of which are endemic to these environments.
 
• The trees in these forests can grow to be quite large and tall, forming multiple layers of vegetation.
 
• Some important tree species found in tropical evergreen forests are rosewood, ebony, and mahogany.
 
• These trees are highly valued for their hardwood and are often used for furniture, construction, and various other applications.
 
• Unfortunately, due to excessive logging and deforestation, many of these tree species have become threatened or endangered.

**In summary, tropical evergreen forests are characterized by their location near the Equator, constant rainfall, thick and dense vegetation, and the presence of valuable hardwood trees such as rosewood, ebony, and mahogany.**

questions.question: What are the drained areas formed by rivers called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Besin**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **besin** is the correct term for the drained areas formed by rivers.
 
• Rivers often drain a specific area of land, which is referred to as a river basin or simply basin.
 
• The term "basin" is commonly used in geography to describe the land area that is drained by a river and its tributaries.
 
• This area is typically bounded by higher land such as hills or mountains.
 
• River basins are important for water management, agriculture, and ecosystems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A **lake** is a large body of water surrounded by land, not specifically related to river drainage.
 
• A **lagoon** is a shallow body of water separated from a larger body of water by a barrier, not directly formed by river drainage.
 
• **Wells** are man-made structures for accessing groundwater and are not related to river drainage areas.

questions.question: In which of the following decade only, India’s Population had shown negative growth?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1911-1921.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The decade 1911-1921 was the only period in India's recorded history when the population showed a negative growth rate.**
 
• **This negative growth was primarily due to the influenza epidemic of 1918, also known as the Spanish Flu, which caused significant mortality.**
 
• **World War I (1914–1918) also contributed to the disruption of resources and widespread hardships, worsening the population decline.**
 
• **During this period, India witnessed widespread famines and epidemics, which significantly impacted the population.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1901-1911:** This decade saw positive population growth despite challenges like famines. The census recorded steady growth due to improved administrative measures and better infrastructure.
 
• **1921-1931:** This decade marked the beginning of steady population growth. Post-1921, India experienced improvements in healthcare and sanitation, which contributed to a rise in population growth rates.
 
• **1931-1941:** The population continued to grow during this period due to advancements in medical facilities, improved public health measures, and agricultural developments despite political unrest during the independence movement.
 
• **Spanish Flu:** A global pandemic that significantly impacted India during the 1918-1920 period, leading to millions of deaths and contributing to the negative growth rate in the 1911-1921 decade.
 
• **Famines:** India faced several famines during the British colonial period, including the Great Bengal Famine of 1943. However, the specific famines during the 1911-1921 decade contributed heavily to population decline.

questions.question: What is the minimum age requirement for a candidate to be elected as a member of the Panchayat Samiti?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The minimum age requirement for a candidate to be elected as a member of the Panchayat Samiti is **21 years**.
 
• The Panchayat Samiti is a rural local government body at the intermediate level in the Panchayati Raj system.
 
• It works for the villages of the tehsil or taluka that together are called a development block.
 
• The Panchayat Samiti is a link between the Gram Panchayat (village council) and the Zila Parishad (district board).
 
• It administers rural development activities and implements schemes for agriculture, rural development, and social welfare.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Panchayati Raj system was introduced in India to decentralize power to the grassroots level.
 
• It was recommended by the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee in 1957 and was constitutionalized through the 73rd Amendment Act of 1992.
 
• The Act provides a three-tier system of Panchayati Raj in every state, namely the Gram Panchayat at the village level, the Panchayat Samiti at the intermediate level, and the Zila Parishad at the district level.
 
• To ensure that the Panchayati Raj institutions function effectively, the Act mandates regular elections every five years.
 
• The Act also provides for the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and women to promote inclusive governance.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Supreme Court :

1. The Supreme Court was established on 26 November 1949, the day India became a Republic.

2. Like its predecessor, the Federal Court of India (1937-1949), it was earlier located in the Chamber of Princes in the Parliament House.

3. It moved to its present building on Mathura Road in New Delhi in 1958.

Which of the following combination is correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **2 and 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

Let's analyze each statement:

 
• **The Supreme Court was established on 26 November 1949, the day India became a Republic.**

 
 
• This statement is **incorrect**.
 
• The Supreme Court of India was established on January 28, 1950, not on November 26, 1949.
 
• The Constitution of India came into force on November 26, 1949, but India officially became a Republic on January 26, 1950, when the Supreme Court replaced the Federal Court of India.
 
 
 
• **Like its predecessor, the Federal Court of India (1937-1949), it was earlier located in the Chamber of Princes in the Parliament House.**
 
 
• This statement is **correct**.
 
• The Supreme Court of India initially functioned from the Chamber of Princes in the Parliament House, just like its predecessor, the Federal Court of India.
 
 
 
• **It moved to its present building on Mathura Road in New Delhi in 1958.**
 
 
• This statement is **correct**.
 
• The Supreme Court of India moved to its present building, which is located on Tilak Marg in New Delhi, in 1958.
 
• The new building was designed by the chief architect of the Government of India, Ganesh Bhikaji Deolalikar.
 
 

So, the correct answer is **2 and 3**.

questions.question: In organic chemistry, which qualitative method is used for testing an unsaturated carbon carbon bond, such as an alkene or alkyne, but NOT for an aromatic carbon-carbon bond?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Bayer's Test__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Baeyer's test** is a chemical test **used to detect the presence of carbon-carbon double bonds or triple bonds in a compound**.
 
• It is **named after** the German chemist, **Adolf von Baeyer**, who developed the test.
 
• The test uses a **solution of potassium permanganate (KMnO₄)**, which is **purple **in color.
 
• When the **potassium permanganate** solution reacts with a compound containing a **carbon-carbon double bond (an alkene) or triple bond (alkyne)**, the solution **changes color from purple to brown**.
 
• The** alkene or alkyne gets oxidized to a glycol **(compound containing two hydroxy groups) during the reaction, which is evidenced by the change in color.
 
• **Baeyer's test** **does not react with aromatic compounds**, where the** carbon-carbon double bonds are part of an aromatic ring**, this allows for differentiation between alkenes/alkynes and aromatic compounds.
 
• The test is simple, quick, and a commonly used laboratory method for the identification of unsaturated hydrocarbons.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Iodoform Test**

 
 
• A pale yellow precipitate of iodoform or triiodomethane is generated when iodine and sodium hydroxide are added to a molecule containing either a methyl ketone or a secondary alcohol with a methyl group in the alpha position. It can be used to distinguish between aldehydes and ketones.
 
 
 
• **Phthalein dye test**
 
 
• When phenol is heated with phthalic anhydride in the presence of concentrated sulfuric acid, a colorless condensation compound known as phenolphthalein is formed. Further reaction with dilute sodium hydroxide solution produces fluorescein, a pink fluorescent compound. Different phenolic compounds produce distinctive colors, which can be seen against a white background.
 
 
 
• **Lucas Test**
 
 
• A solution of anhydrous zinc chloride in concentrated hydrochloric acid is used in the Lucas test to differentiate and categorize primary, secondary, and tertiary alcohols. This solution is known colloquially as the Lucas reagent.
 
 
 
• Alkaline **KMnO4** acts as **Bayers reagent **which involves the reduction of the permanganate ion (MnO4-) to manganese dioxide (MnO2), while the alkene is oxidized to form the 1,2-diol.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9eaa48ad108755e9cba0a734ba3c3f6cc2cf9725e8d663372adbd17d6e78ca17.png] 

 
• 1,2-diol undergoes rearrangement and then oxidised to carboxylic acid in the presence of alk.KMnO4. Alk. KMnO4 acts as strong oxidizing agent which involves conversion of alcohol, aldehydes and ketones to their corresponding carboxylic acids.

questions.question: Warren Hastings’ experiment of auctioning the right to collect revenue to the highest bidder is almost similar to
questions.solution:
Warren Hastings’ experiment of auctioning the right to collect revenue to the highest bidder is almost similar to __**Ijara system of the Mughals.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Warren Hastings**, the Governor-General of British India from 1773 to 1785, implemented an experiment known as the auctioning of the right to collect revenue.
 
• Under this system, the British East India Company would auction off the revenue-collecting rights of a specific region to the** highest bidder.**
 
• The **Ijara system,** on the other hand, was a revenue collection system used by the Mughal Empire in India.
 
• In the Ijara system, the **Mughal rulers** would lease out revenue collection rights to individuals or groups, who were responsible for collecting and remitting a fixed amount of revenue from a particular region.
 
• While there are similarities between Hastings' auctioning system and the Ijara system, they differ in certain key aspects.
 
• Both systems involved leasing revenue collection rights, but the mechanisms and objectives were distinct.
 
• **Hastings' auction system** aimed to maximize revenue for the British East India Company.
 
• The highest bidder won the rights to collect revenue and was expected to pay the bid amount upfront, making it a competitive process focused on generating immediate income for the Company.
 
• In contrast, the Ijara system of the Mughals focused on stability and regular revenue collection.
 
• The** leaseholders** in the Ijara system were responsible for maintaining law and order in their assigned regions and ensuring the smooth collection of revenue.
 
• Their role was not solely profit-oriented but involved broader governance responsibilities.
 
• 
 
Therefore, while there may be similarities between Hastings' auctioning system and the Ijara system of the Mughals in terms of revenue collection through leasing rights, their underlying objectives and mechanisms differed significantly.

 

Thus we conclude that Warren Hastings’ experiment of auctioning the right to collect revenue to the highest bidder is almost similar to **Ijara system of the Mughals.**__

• The Queen's Proclamation of 1858, also known as the "Proclamation by the Queen in Council," marked the formal transfer of power from the East India Company to the British Crown.
 
• It is referred to as the "Magna Carta of the Indian people" because it promised equal treatment of Indian subjects and British citizens under the law.
 
• The proclamation assured non-interference in religious practices and customs, which was a significant step toward addressing Indian grievances post the Revolt of 1857.
 
• Queen Victoria declared that Indians would be eligible for government positions based on their education and ability, promoting a sense of fairness.
 
• The proclamation was issued on November 1, 1858, and was read by Lord Canning, the first Viceroy of India, in Allahabad.

• **Indian Councils Act of 1861:**
 
 
• This act marked the beginning of legislative reforms in India under British rule.
 
• It introduced the concept of non-official Indian members in the legislative council.
 
 
 
• **Charter Act of 1833:**
 
 
• This act centralized administrative power by making the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India.

• **Treaty of Allahabad (1765):**

questions.question: Which of the following problems related to Indian agriculture is caused by erratic monsoon patterns?

options.text: Inadequate use of modern farming technology

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Erratic Monsoon Patterns:**

 
 
• Monsoon patterns in India are often unpredictable and can vary significantly from year to year, leading to severe consequences for agriculture.
 
• Dependence on monsoon rains makes Indian agriculture highly vulnerable to the inconsistencies of the monsoon season.
 
 
 
• **Crop Failures:**
 
 
• Erratic monsoons can lead to either insufficient or excessive rainfall, both of which can cause crop failures.
 
• Inadequate rainfall results in drought-like conditions, affecting the sowing of crops and reducing yields.
 
• Excessive rainfall can lead to flooding, damaging crops and leading to significant losses for farmers.
 
 
 
• **Poor Water Supply for Irrigation:**
 
 
• The unpredictability of the monsoon affects water availability in reservoirs, rivers, and groundwater sources.
 
• This results in insufficient water for irrigation, which is crucial for crop growth, especially in regions that do not have reliable irrigation infrastructure.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Inadequate use of modern farming technology:**

 
 
• This is not directly caused by erratic monsoon patterns. It is more related to factors like lack of awareness, financial constraints, and limited access to modern technology.
 
 
 
• **High productivity in rainfed areas:**
 
 
• This option is incorrect as erratic monsoon patterns generally lead to reduced productivity in rainfed areas due to unpredictable water supply.
 
 
 
• **Low yield in irrigated areas:**
 
 
• This issue is less likely to be directly caused by erratic monsoons. Irrigated areas usually have alternative water sources to manage crop growth, even if monsoon patterns are unpredictable.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• India’s agriculture is heavily dependent on the monsoon season, which usually spans from June to September.
 
• Approximately 60% of the country’s farmland is rainfed, highlighting the critical importance of monsoon rains for crop production.
 
• Government initiatives and policies are often focused on improving irrigation facilities and promoting water conservation techniques to mitigate the impact of erratic monsoons.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding water remaining colder in an earthen pot (matka)?

options.text: Water gets evaporated at the surface of the earthen pot.

The water oozes out through the pores in an earthen pot.

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Water gets evaporated at the surface of the earthen pot:** The evaporation process helps in cooling the water inside the pot.
 
• **The earthen pot is porous:** The porous nature of the pot allows water to seep through and evaporate, aiding in the cooling effect.
 
• **The water oozes out through the pores in an earthen pot:** This oozing water evaporates from the surface, taking away heat from the water inside and thus keeping it cool.
 
• **Environmental water vapour does not enter the pot through pores:** The cooling mechanism is due to the evaporation of water from inside the pot, not due to external water vapor entering through the pores.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Porous Nature:** The earthen pot is made of clay that has tiny holes or pores which allow water to seep through. This characteristic is crucial for the cooling process.
 
• **Cooling Mechanism:** The continuous evaporation of water from the surface of the pot leads to a cooling effect. This is because the evaporation process requires heat, which is taken from the water inside the pot, thus lowering its temperature.
 
• **Heat Transfer:** The process of heat transfer during evaporation involves the removal of heat from the water inside the pot, making it cooler compared to the external environment.

questions.question: Which of the following metals is more reactive towards dilute hydrochloric acid?
questions.solution:

__
 
• Magnesium (Mg) is more reactive towards dilute hydrochloric acid compared to aluminum (Al), zinc (Zn), and iron (Fe).
 
• When magnesium reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid, it produces hydrogen gas and forms magnesium chloride:
 
• {Mg} + 2{HCl} rightarrow {MgCl}₂ + {H}₂ 
 
• This reaction is faster and more vigorous than the reactions of Al, Zn, and Fe with dilute hydrochloric acid.
 
• Magnesium is higher in the reactivity series compared to aluminum, zinc, and iron, making it more reactive.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reactivity Series**

 
 
• The reactivity series is a series of metals arranged in order of decreasing reactivity.
 
• It helps to predict how metals will react with acids, water, and other substances.
 
 
 
• **Hydrogen Gas Test**
 
 
• Hydrogen gas can be tested by bringing a lit splint near the mouth of the test tube; a 'pop' sound confirms the presence of hydrogen.
 
 
 
• **Reactions of Other Metals**
 
 
• Aluminum reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid to form aluminum chloride and hydrogen gas, but it is less vigorous due to the formation of a protective oxide layer.
 
• Zinc reacts more readily than iron but less than magnesium, forming zinc chloride and hydrogen gas.
 
• Iron reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid to form iron(II) chloride and hydrogen gas, but the reaction is slower compared to magnesium and zinc.

__

questions.question: A pump can fill a tank with water in 2 hours. Because of a leak, it takes 6 hours to fill the tank. The leak can drain all the water from the tank in:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

If a pump fills a tank in x hours and with a leak takes y hours, the time taken by the leak to empty the tank is given by:

Time = (x × y) ÷ (y − x)

Here, x = 2 hours and y = 6 hours.

Time = (2 × 6) ÷ (6 − 2) = 12 ÷ 4 = 3 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 hours.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Pump to fill the tank = 2 hours

Time taken by Pump + Leak to fill the tank = 6 hours

**Method Used:**

We use the LCM method to find the total capacity of the tank and the efficiency of the pump and the leak.

 
 

 **Component**
 **Time (hours)**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 Pump

 6 ÷ 6 = 1
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of Pump + Efficiency of Leak = Combined Efficiency

⇒ 3 + Efficiency of Leak = 1

⇒ Efficiency of Leak = 1 − 3 = −2 units/hour

⇒ The negative sign indicates that the leak is emptying the tank at a rate of 2 units/hour.

⇒ Time taken by the leak to empty the full tank = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of Leak

⇒ Time = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 3 hours.**

**__Additional Information__**

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

An inlet pipe fills the tank (doing positive work), whereas an outlet pipe or a leak empties it (doing negative work).

Pipes & Cisterns Formula

If a pipe fills a tank in A hours and another empties it in B hours (where B > A), the net part filled in 1 hour is (1 ÷ A − 1 ÷ B).

Combined Work Efficiency

Combined efficiency is the algebraic sum of the individual efficiencies: ETₒₜₐₗ = E₁ + E₂ − E₃ (where E₃ represents an emptying pipe or leak).

questions.question: There are some friends, all less than 20 years. When paired amongst themselves they realize that the sum of their ages is a multiple of 5 . If their ages are distinct prime numbers, then the number of possible pairs are:

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Prime numbers less than 20: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19.

For sum to be divisible by 5, group primes by their remainder when divided by 5.

Remainder 1 {11} & Remainder 4 {19} → 1 × 1 = 1 pair.

Remainder 2 {2, 7, 17} & Remainder 3 {3, 13} → 3 × 2 = 6 pairs.

Total possible pairs = 1 + 6 = 7.

**∴ The correct answer is 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ages are distinct prime numbers less than 20.

Sum of a pair of ages is a multiple of 5.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime numbers less than 20 are: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19

⇒ Now, we check distinct pairs (a, b) such that (a + b) is a multiple of 5 (i.e., 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30...)

⇒ Pairs with sum = 5: (2, 3) → 1 pair

⇒ Pairs with sum = 10: (3, 7) → 1 pair

⇒ Pairs with sum = 15: (2, 13) → 1 pair

⇒ Pairs with sum = 20: (3, 17) and (7, 13) → 2 pairs

⇒ Pairs with sum = 25: None

⇒ Pairs with sum = 30: (11, 19) and (13, 17) → 2 pairs

Total students (N) = 30. The median lies at the (N/2) = 15th position.

Cumulative frequencies: 2, 5, 13, 19... The 15th value falls in the 55-60 class.

Median = L + [(N/2 − cf) ÷ f] × h

**Given:**

Weight classes (in kg): 40-45, 45-50, 50-55, 55-60, 60-65, 65-70, 70-75

Number of students (f): 2, 3, 8, 6, 6, 3, 2

**Formula Used:**

Median = l + [ (N/2 − cf) ÷ f ] × h

Where l = lower limit of median class, N = total frequency, cf = cumulative frequency of the class preceding the median class, f = frequency of the median class, h = class size.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Finding Cumulative Frequencies (cf):

⇒ 40-45 : f = 2, cf = 2

⇒ 45-50 : f = 3, cf = 2 + 3 = 5

⇒ 50-55 : f = 8, cf = 5 + 8 = 13

⇒ 55-60 : f = 6, cf = 13 + 6 = 19 (Median Class)

⇒ 60-65 : f = 6, cf = 19 + 6 = 25

⇒ 65-70 : f = 3, cf = 25 + 3 = 28

⇒ 70-75 : f = 2, cf = 28 + 2 = 30

⇒ Total frequency N = 30, so N/2 = 15.

⇒ The cumulative frequency just greater than 15 is 19, which corresponds to the class interval 55-60.

⇒ l = 55, cf = 13, f = 6, h = 5

⇒ Median = 55 + [ (15 − 13) ÷ 6 ] × 5

⇒ Median = 55 + [ 2 ÷ 6 ] × 5

⇒ Median = 55 + [ 1 ÷ 3 ] × 5

⇒ Median = 55 + 1.666...

⇒ Median ≈ 56.67

**∴ The correct answer is 56.67 kg.**

**__Additional Information__**

Mode of Grouped Data

Mode = l + [ (f₁ − f₀) ÷ (2f₁ − f₀ − f₂) ] × h, where f₁ is the frequency of the modal class.

Mean of Grouped Data

Mean = Σ(fᵢ × xᵢ) ÷ Σfᵢ, where xᵢ is the class mark (mid-point) of each interval.

Empirical Relationship

Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean. This formula connects the three main measures of central tendency.

questions.question: A team of 30 men is supposed to complete a work in 41 days. After 25 days, 6 more men are employed, and the work is finished one day earlier. By how many days would it have been delayed, if 6 more men were not employed?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the work finished 1 day earlier than the 41-day schedule, it finished in 40 days.

The remaining work after 25 days was completed by 36 men in 15 days (40 − 25 = 15).

Total remaining work = 36 × 15 = 540 man-days.

If only the original 30 men worked, time taken for remaining work = 540 ÷ 30 = 18 days.

Initial scheduled time for the remaining work = 41 − 25 = 16 days.

Delay = Time taken by 30 men − Scheduled time = 18 − 16 = 2 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial number of men = 30

Scheduled time to complete work = 41 days

Number of days worked by 30 men = 25 days

Extra men added after 25 days = 6

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Number of Men × Number of Days

**Calculation:**

⇒ Actual time taken to finish the work = 41 − 1 = 40 days

⇒ Days worked by the new group of men = 40 − 25 = 15 days

⇒ Total men working in the last 15 days = 30 + 6 = 36 men

⇒ Remaining work completed by 36 men = 36 × 15 = 540 units

⇒ If no extra men were added, time taken by 30 men to complete 540 units = 540 ÷ 30 = 18 days

⇒ Total days taken if no extra men were added = 25 + 18 = 43 days

⇒ Delay = Total days taken − Scheduled days

⇒ Delay = 43 − 41 = 2 days

**∴ The correct answer is 2 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Chain Rule (MDH Concept)

For a group of men working, the relation between Men (M), Days (D), Hours (H) and Work (W) is given by: (M₁ × D₁ × H₁) ÷ W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂) ÷ W₂.

Efficiency & Time Relationship

The efficiency of a worker is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete the work. If efficiency ratio of A and B is x:y, their time taken ratio will be y:x.

Total Work Formula

Total work can be assumed as the LCM of the days taken by individuals, and it is calculated as Total Work = Efficiency × Time Taken.
</p

Time to meet = Remaining Distance ÷ Relative Speed

**Calculations:**

Let the total distance between Delhi and Jainagar be D.

⇒ Time taken by Train 1 = 10:00 a.m. − 6:00 a.m. = 4 hours.

⇒ Time taken by Train 2 = 11:30 a.m. − 8:00 a.m. = 3.5 hours = 7/2 hours.

⇒ Speed of Train 1 = D/4

⇒ Speed of Train 2 = D ÷ (7/2) = 2D/7

⇒ By 8:00 a.m., Train 1 travels for 2 hours (6:00 a.m. to 8:00 a.m.).

⇒ Distance covered by Train 1 = 2 × (D/4) = D/2

⇒ Remaining distance at 8:00 a.m. = D − D/2 = D/2

Now, both trains are moving towards each other.

⇒ Relative speed = D/4 + 2D/7 = (7D + 8D) / 28 = 15D/28

⇒ Time taken to meet = (D/2) ÷ (15D/28)

⇒ Time taken = (D/2) × (28/15D) = 14/15 hours.

⇒ Convert 14/15 hours into minutes: 14/15 × 60 = 56 minutes.

⇒ The trains meet 56 minutes after 8:00 a.m., which is 8:56 a.m.

**∴ The correct answer is 8:56 a.m.**

Relative Speed Concept

When two bodies travel in opposite directions at speeds S₁ and S₂, their relative speed is S₁ + S₂. Time to meet = Distance between them ÷ Relative Speed.

Direct Formula for Meeting Time

If Train 1 takes time T₁, Train 2 takes time T₂, and Train 1 starts Δt hours early, the time to meet after Train 2 starts is: Time = (T₁ − Δt) × T₂ ÷ (T₁ + T₂).

LCM Method for Constant Distance

When only travel times are given for a fixed distance, assuming the total distance as the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the given times entirely eliminates fractional calculations and speeds up the process.

questions.question: On dividing 4⁹⁹⁹ to 7 what will the remainder be?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By Fermat's Little Theorem, ap−¹ leaves a remainder of 1 when divided by a prime p.

Here, a = 4 and p = 7. Thus, 4⁶ leaves a remainder of 1 when divided by 7.

We can split the given power as: 999 = 6 × 166 + 3.

So, 4⁹⁹⁹ = (4⁶)¹⁶⁶ × 4³.

Remainder = 1¹⁶⁶ × 64 = 64. When 64 is divided by 7, the remainder is 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: 4⁹⁹⁹ ÷ 7

**Method Used:**

Binomial Expansion Remainder Theorem

**Calculations:**

⇒ Express 4⁹⁹⁹ in terms of 4³, as 4³ = 64 (which is 63 + 1).

⇒ 4⁹⁹⁹ = (4³)³³³

⇒ Substituting 4³ = 64, we get 64³³³ ÷ 7.

⇒ Split 64 as (63 + 1), since 63 is a multiple of 7.

⇒ Expression: (63 + 1)³³³ ÷ 7

⇒ Using remainder theorem, (ax + k)ⁿ ÷ a leaves remainder kⁿ.

⇒ Remainder = 1³³³ = 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Binomial Remainder Theorem

When (ax + k)ⁿ is divided by a, the remainder is always kⁿ. Similarly, (ax − 1)ⁿ divided by a leaves remainder 1 if n is even, and a−1 if n is odd.

Fermat's Little Theorem

If p is a prime number and a is not divisible by p, then ap−¹ leaves a remainder of 1 when divided by p. This provides an alternative fast method for remainder questions.

Concept of Cyclicity

The remainders of powers of a number divided by a fixed divisor follow a repeating cycle. Finding this cycle length allows simplification of massive exponents.
</p

questions.question: Simplify (7x - 1)³ + (7x + 1)³.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Use the direct algebraic identity: (a − b)³ + (a + b)³ = 2a³ + 6ab².

Here, substitute a = 7x and b = 1.

⇒ 2(7x)³ + 6(7x)(1)²

⇒ 2(343x³) + 42x

⇒ 686x³ + 42x

**∴ The correct answer is 686x³ + 42x.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The expression is (7x − 1)³ + (7x + 1)³.

**Formula Used:**

(a + b)³ = a³ + b³ + 3a²b + 3ab²

(a − b)³ = a³ − b³ − 3a²b + 3ab²

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let us expand both terms individually using the formulas.

⇒ (7x − 1)³ = (7x)³ − 1³ − 3(7x)²(1) + 3(7x)(1)²

⇒ (7x − 1)³ = 343x³ − 1 − 147x² + 21x

⇒ (7x + 1)³ = (7x)³ + 1³ + 3(7x)²(1) + 3(7x)(1)²

⇒ (7x + 1)³ = 343x³ + 1 + 147x² + 21x

⇒ Now, add the two expanded forms together:

⇒ (343x³ − 1 − 147x² + 21x) + (343x³ + 1 + 147x² + 21x)

⇒ The terms with opposite signs cancel out (−1 and +1, −147x² and +147x²).

⇒ = (343x³ + 343x³) + (21x + 21x)

⇒ = 686x³ + 42x

**∴ The correct answer is 686x³ + 42x.**

**__Additional Information__**

Sum and Difference of Cubes

Basic algebraic identities are: a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²) and a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²).

Algebraic Identities for Squares

Similarly, for squares: (a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²) and (a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab.

Cubes Subtraction Trick

Similar to the sum of cubes, the difference expression can be simplified directly as: (a + b)³ − (a − b)³ = 2b³ + 6a²b.
</p

LCM & HCF of Two Numbers

For any two numbers, the product of the numbers is strictly equal to the product of their HCF and LCM (i.e., a × b = HCF × LCM). However, this direct rule is generally not applicable to three or more numbers.

questions.question: If cot 75° = 2 - √3 Find the value of cot 15°
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

We know the complementary angle property: tan θ = cot(90° − θ).

⇒ tan 15° = cot(90° − 15°) = cot 75° = 2 − √3

We also know that cot θ = 1 ÷ tan θ.

⇒ cot 15° = 1 ÷ (2 − √3)

Rationalizing the denominator by multiplying with its conjugate (2 + √3):

⇒ cot 15° = (2 + √3) ÷ (2² − (√3)²) = (2 + √3) ÷ (4 − 3) = 2 + √3

**∴ The correct answer is 2 + √3.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

cot 75° = 2 − √3

**Formula Used:**

cot(A − B) = (cot A × cot B + 1) ÷ (cot B − cot A)

**Calculation:**

We can write 15° as (45° − 30°).

⇒ cot 15° = cot(45° − 30°)

⇒ cot 15° = (cot 45° × cot 30° + 1) ÷ (cot 30° − cot 45°)

Substitute the standard trigonometric values (cot 45° = 1 and cot 30° = √3):

⇒ cot 15° = (1 × √3 + 1) ÷ (√3 − 1)

⇒ cot 15° = (√3 + 1) ÷ (√3 − 1)

To rationalize, multiply both the numerator and the denominator by (√3 + 1):

⇒ cot 15° = [(√3 + 1) × (√3 + 1)] ÷ [(√3 − 1) × (√3 + 1)]

⇒ cot 15° = (3 + 1 + 2√3) ÷ (3 − 1)

⇒ cot 15° = (4 + 2√3) ÷ 2

⇒ cot 15° = 2 × (2 + √3) ÷ 2

⇒ cot 15° = 2 + √3

**∴ The correct answer is 2 + √3.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios of Complementary Angles

Two angles are complementary if their sum is exactly 90°. Key relations include: sin(90° − θ) = cos θ, tan(90° − θ) = cot θ, and sec(90° − θ) = cosec θ.

Important Values for 15° and 75°

sin 15° = cos 75° = (√6 − √2) ÷ 4 
 cos 15° = sin 75° = (√6 + √2) ÷ 4 
 tan 15° = cot 75° = 2 − √3 
 cot 15° = tan 75° = 2 + √3

Rationalization Rule

When a denominator contains a surd of the form (a − √b), it can be eliminated by multiplying both the numerator and the denominator by its conjugate pair (a + √b) based on the algebraic identity (x − y)(x + y) = x² − y².
</p

questions.question: The difference between cost price and selling price is Rs. 672. If loss percentage is 21 percent, then what is the selling price?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

In case of a loss, the difference between Cost Price (CP) and Selling Price (SP) is the loss itself.

Given the loss is 21%, it corresponds to Rs. 672.

Selling Price corresponds to (100% − 21%) = 79% of CP.

SP = (672 ÷ 21) × 79 = 32 × 79 = 2528.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 2528.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Difference between CP and SP (Loss) = Rs. 672

Loss percentage = 21%

**Formula Used:**

Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100

SP = CP − Loss

 
 Selling Price = 79%
 ? (Rs. 2528)
 
 Loss = 21%
 Rs. 672
 

 Cost Price (CP) = 100%

**Calculations:**

⇒ 21% of CP = 672

⇒ (21 ÷ 100) × CP = 672

⇒ CP = (672 × 100) ÷ 21

⇒ CP = 32 × 100 = 3200

⇒ SP = CP − Loss

⇒ SP = 3200 − 672 = 2528

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 2528.**

**__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit occurs when the Selling Price (SP) is greater than the Cost Price (CP), while a loss occurs when SP is less than CP. Both are calculated based on the Cost Price unless specified otherwise.

Selling Price Calculation

When there is a loss, the Selling Price can be found directly using the multiplier formula: SP = CP × (100 − Loss%) ÷ 100.

Ratio Approach

If loss is given as a percentage L%, CP is always taken as 100 units. The loss represents L units, and the SP represents (100 − L) units. Using this unitary method simplifies calculations directly without finding CP first.
</p

questions.question: Four years ago, the average age of a group of five members was 38 years. One more man joins the group and the present average age of the group members becomes 44 years. What is the present age (in years) of the new member?

Present average age of the 5 members = 38 + 4 = 42 years.

New average age of the 6 members = 44 years.

Age of new member = New Average + Old Members × Increase in Average

Age of new member = 44 + 5 × (44 − 42)

Age of new member = 44 + 10 = 54 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 54 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ Present average age of 6 members (with new member) = 44 years

 Present Ages Representation

 5 Members' Present Age = 210
 New: 54
 

 Total 6 Members' Present Age = 264

**Calculations:**

⇒ Present average age of the initial 5 members = 38 + 4 = 42 years

⇒ Present sum of ages of these 5 members = 5 × 42 = 210 years

⇒ Present sum of ages of all 6 members = 6 × 44 = 264 years

⇒ Present age of the new member = 264 − 210 = 54 years

Concept of Age Progression

If the average age of a group is A years, then after t years, the average age of the same group becomes A + t years, provided no members are added or removed.

Inclusion of a New Member

Weighted Average

When two groups with n₁ and n₂ members and averages A₁ and A₂ are mixed, the combined average is (n₁ × A₁ + n₂ × A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).
</p
